B3: Wave compaction amnesia – promote T2.5 (PreCompact Mnemos) to Wave 0 to protect executor state before context compaction hits

validation_of_gpt55_findings.finding: B1: T‑1 SQLite quiesce – use `.backup` command for atomic snapshot, not raw `tar` of WAL‑mode DB
B2: T‑1 extended backup scope – inventory external state (Keychain, LaunchAgents, npm, MCP registry) for rollback
B3: T1.2 guardrails missing SQL destructive patterns (UPDATE, DELETE, INSERT, TRUNCATE without TABLE), MultiEdit tool, and cURL‑pipe‑to‑shell bypass
B4: T3.2 Postgres MCP password leak – never export `PGPASSWORD` globally; use a scoped wrapper that fetches from Keychain per invocation
B5: T2.5 Mnemos anti‑hallucination – parse structured `tool_use`/`tool_result` pairs from JSONL, check `exit_code`; separate `attempted_commands` from `successful_commands`
Code review #1 – `set -euo pipefail` was missing `-e` in T-1 and G3
Code review #2 – `pipefail` missing, causing tar errors to be swallowed

new_issues_post_integration.description: G3 rollback does not restore the SQLite snapshot to the live `memory.db`. T-1 now backs up a snapshot file (`.claude/memory.db.snapshot-${DATE}`) instead of the raw DB, but G3 merely extracts the backup tarball without later copying the snapshot over the live `memory.db`. Consequently a full rollback leaves the old (possibly corrupt) live DB unchanged.
new_issues_post_integration.recommendation: Add a step in G3 Phase 4 (after tar extraction) to copy the snapshot to the real path: `cp .claude/memory.db.snapshot-* .claude/memory.db`.

new_issues_post_integration.description: T-1 backup `tar` command is missing `--ignore-missing` (or equivalent). The script runs with `set -euo pipefail`, and several listed paths (`~/.claude/state/`, certain LaunchAgent plists, `~/.config/nuzantara/`, etc.) may not exist at backup time. This will cause the entire T-1 backup to fail early, potentially blocking all subsequent waves.
new_issues_post_integration.recommendation: Add `--no-error-if-missing` / `--ignore-failed-read` flag (macOS `tar` uses `--no-recursion` but better to wrap in a loop that collects existing files) or explicitly allow missing files with a pre-check.

new_issues_post_integration.description: T3.2 post‑integration fallback for storing the read‑only password: `security add-generic-password … -w "$PG_PASSWORD_RO"` would expose the generated password as a command‑line argument in `ps` output. The spec itself documents this fallback, but the integration should either remove it or strictly avoid it.
new_issues_post_integration.recommendation: Remove the fallback entirely; the‑stdin method (`-w -`) is sufficient on modern macOS. If a fallback is truly necessary, wrap in a Python helper that calls Security.framework.

regressions_from_fixes.description: The T-1 backup script now attempts to back up several extended‑scope paths (e.g., `~/.claude/state/`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.config/nuzantara/`) that may not exist or may contain sensitive data. While the extended scope itself is a good addition (from GPT-5.5 B2), the script does not gracefully handle missing files, which breaks the bullet‑proof pre‑execution backup assumption.

missing_still: G3 rollback must explicitly restore the SQLite snapshot to the live DB path (NI-1).
T-1 backup must tolerate missing files to avoid failing the entire pre‑execution step (NI-2).
The password fallback in T3.2 should be eliminated to avoid process‑listing exposure (NI-3).
G1 gate currently only checks nuzantara‑rag health; after Wave 2 it should be expanded to verify the other MCP servers that were installed (postgres, github, vercel) to match the full spec scope.
honest_admission: In my first‑pass DeepSeek review I identified 3 blockers and 12 concerns, but I completely missed: (a) the SQLite WAL safety issue when rolling back the memory database; (b) the necessity of an executor state manifest to survive context compaction; (c) the external state rollback dimension (Postgres roles, Keychain, MCP registry); (d) the late placement of T2.5 which would let compaction destroy executor state before Wave 2; (e) the hard‑coded secret‑in‑plist anti‑pattern in G4; (f) the missing guardrail patterns for MultiEdit and advanced SQL statements; (g) the subtle tar failure mode due to missing files; and (h) the password exposure via process arguments in T3.2. Gemini and GPT-5.5 each caught critical classes of bugs that I overlooked, and their fixes have been integrated mostly correctly, but a few new regressions (notably the snapshot restoration gap and backup fragility) were introduced during integration.
